text:
mike_sre: Heads up — Kibana counts for req_id queries in us-west1 are drifting vs us-east after last night's rollout. Looks like ~6% fewer hits in west for gpu-backed requests. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

jamie_prod: Seeing the same on the per-route SLO dashboard. Grafana shows a small spike in egress errors around 02:11 UTC.

alexa_obs: Added some quick Loki queries, results look aligned with the Kibana delta. Possibly sampling/ingest drop?

samir_sre: Can you paste the Kibana query you used? I want to cross-check with the raw Loki streams.

mike_sre: Sure — here's what I ran in Kibana (truncated):

```
req_id:"*" AND environment:prod AND gpu:true AND @timestamp:[now-1h TO now]
| stats count() by req_id
```

jamie_prod: And Loki for raw logs: 

```
{job="gpu-ingest"} |= "req_id" | json | req_id="*" | line_format "{req_id}"
| count_over_time({job="gpu-ingest"}[1h])
```

alexa_obs: On the Grafana side the panel for "egress 5xx" shows a short window where us-west1 egress RPS dropped then error rate rose. Could be cloud provider NAT gateway or egress throttling.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/2026-03-12-asm completed in us-west1 at 02:08:45 UTC (canary->100%).

mike_sre: Timeline matches the rollout. But why would counts be missing only for GPU-tagged requests? We didn't change the routing logic.

tess_infra: Quick idea: the GPU pool pods send logs to a sidecar that forwards to loki via an egress path that uses a NAT. If NAT connection table hit limits we might silently drop TCP connections and counts won't reach central ingest.

samir_sre: I pulled a flent of the node-level conntrack metrics — here's the prom query I ran: `sum(conntrack_entries{zone="us-west1"}) by (instance)` — showing a bump at 02:10.

mike_sre: Any kube events on the gpu nodes?

alexa_obs: I ran: 

```
kubectl get events -n infra --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Node --since=15m
```

and saw repeated `FailedDelete` on NAT gateway annotation. Also a few `NetworkPolicy` deny logs from the egress-proxy.

jamie_prod: Loki raw lines around the time include `error=connection reset by peer` and `error=write: broken pipe` from the forwarder.

mike_sre: So forwarder losing connection -> logs not ingested -> Kibana counts drop. But why only gpu requests? Because GPU sidecar uses an older forwarder image with lower connection pooling.

tess_infra: That would explain it. We have two forwarder images in prod: `fwdr:v1.3` on GPU nodes and `fwdr:v1.5` on CPU nodes. v1.3 doesn't use HTTP/2 multiplexing and opens lots of short connections. Under NAT ephemeral exhaustion it drops.

samir_sre: Confirmed. `kubectl -n ml describe ds gpu-log-forwarder` shows image `fwdr:v1.3`.

mike_sre: Action items: (1) patch ds to v1.5 in us-west1, (2) increase node conntrack on us-west NATs as stopgap, (3) add alert for per-pool ingestion drop so we catch this earlier.

alexa_obs: I'll open a quick PR to bump the DaemonSet. Also adding a Grafana per-pool ingest rate panel.

jamie_prod: For immediate triage, can we re-route GPU forwarders to the alternative egress subnet with more NAT capacity?

tess_infra: We can, but that's a config change on the node pool and needs careful rollout. I'll schedule a manual reroute for tonight if needed.

oncall-bot: incident:ingest-drop created (sev:low) — assigned to samir_sre and tess_infra.

samir_sre: I've also tuned Loki ingestion alert threshold — it was global and too coarse. New rule: alert when gpu-ingest_lines_rate drops by >5% for 10m compared to 1h baseline.

mike_sre: Good. Do we want a short postmortem? Looks like low-impact but could recur when we scale GPUs.

jamie_prod: Yes — add notes about forwarder image, conntrack limits, and rollout timing. I'll draft.

alexa_obs: One more note: Kibana queries that rely on rollup or index patterns may exaggerate diffs because of sampling — raw-loki cross-check should be part of the runbook. Adding that to the triage doc.

tess_infra: Patch is in canary now (`fwdr:v1.5`), canary logs look stable and no connection resets. Rolling to the rest of the ds in 5m.

mike_sre: Awesome. Once rolled, let's re-run the Kibana vs Loki counts job for the last 2h and close the incident if counts align. :thumbsup:

samir_sre: Will do — running comparison job now. If anyone wants the query glue I used, open thread in #eng-sre-tools and I'll paste.

mike_sre: Thanks all. Leaving this thread open until postmortem and counts validated.
